messages:
emily-support: Customer ACME just flagged a production incident — UI shows region eu-west-1 but their requests are hitting us-east-1 and they see 300-500ms extra tail latency + occasional 401s. They attached a request sample and a screenshot of the console region badge.
emily-support: cURL they sent (sanitized):
```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \n  -H 'X-Client-ID: acme-123' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
emily-support: Response headers from the customer (copied):
```
x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d
date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 15:42:10 GMT
server: redwood-prod
x-serving-region: us-east-1
content-length: 123
```
emily-support: Console shows project->region: eu-west-1 (screenshot) but `x-serving-region` is us-east-1. Customer is understandably upset. Can someone triage? :exclamation:

raj-eng: Thanks Emily. Can you paste the full `x-routing-info` and the request trace id? Also which org/team?
emily-support: Trace id: `r-0a1b2c3d`. Org: acme-inc. I asked them to include `x-routing-info` but they only had `x-serving-region`. I told them to resend full headers, but they said it happens consistently for them since ~10:30 UTC.

megan-sre: Pulling traces for r-0a1b2c3d now. Initial summary: request arrived at edge in eu-west-1 but the routing service selected a fallback host in us-east-1 due to a mismatch in the POP-to-capacity mapping for acme-inc. See routing log snippet: 
```
[15:42:09.812] TRACE r-0a1b2c3d pop_lookup: preferred_pop=eu-west-1, lookup_cache=MISS
[15:42:09.813] TRACE r-0a1b2c3d route_select: candidate_pops=[eu-west-1, us-east-1], capacity_check: eu-west-1=overcommitted -> fallback_to=us-east-1, fallback_reason=capacity
[15:42:09.813] TRACE r-0a1b2c3d proxy_connect: upstream=us-east-1-host42.redwood.internal
```
megan-sre: That explains the extra latency. The 401s likely from token verification hitting a different auth cluster (regional KMS/HSM boundaries).

luis-telemetry: I dug into the routing cache. For acme-inc the pop mapping entry had an incorrect `tag` value after an automated infra migration last week — cache TTL renewal failed and the node fell back to global defaults. The routing-bot also flagged a cache-invalidation error at 10:28 UTC: `pop-cache-refresh failed: 504 from control-plane` (see attached).

luis-telemetry: Action taken: flushed the routing cache for acme-inc and forced a sync with control-plane. I also deployed a hotfix that makes lookup-cache MISSes fallback to attempting a second-choice within the same region before cross-region fallback.

routing-bot: automated: pop-cache-refresh for org=acme-inc completed (status=OK) at 15:44:02 UTC.

megan-sre: After the cache flush I replayed the trace — subsequent requests for the same trace id are now routed to `eu-west-1-host17` and `x-serving-region` matches console: `eu-west-1`. Latency back to expected baseline.

emily-support: Great. I messaged the customer with interim update and asked them to retry. They want to know root cause and whether they'll see this again.

luis-telemetry: Root cause summary for support message: control-plane migration left a small set of routing entries with stale tag values; cache TTL refresh failed due to intermittent 504s to control-plane, causing some orgs to inherit global defaults which prefer capacity-available hosts (often cross-region). Hotfix prevents immediate cross-region fallback on miss. Full fix: we need a control-plane retry/backoff improvement and better visibility in Console (see product suggestion).

raj-eng: Notes for follow-up and ticket: 1) Offer customers a one-time credit for impacted window (agreed). 2) SRE to submit postmortem with timeline + control-plane retry fix ETA (assigned to me). 3) Product: expose "actual serving region" in the Console request logs and add an org-level "pin-region" option to avoid automatic cross-region fallback for regulated customers.

megan-sre: Quick repro steps for internal QA:
1) create org test-pop-miss with preferred_pop=eu-west-1
2) patch control-plane to return 504 for pop-cache-refresh for that org
3) send 50 parallel requests and observe routing log showing `fallback_to=us-east-1`
4) apply cache flush & hotfix, verify subsequent requests route to eu-west-1

raj-eng: Thanks. I'll file the internal incident ticket and loop in product. Emily — can you follow up with Acme and close the customer loop after they confirm retries? Also capture any request samples if they still happen.

emily-support: Will do. I'll offer credit and let them know the mitigation and planned product change. :thumbsup:

luis-telemetry: Follow-ups for infra: I'll open a control-plane backlog item for retry/backoff metrics, and add an alert for `pop-cache-refresh` failure rate > 0.5% (to avoid silent TTL expiry).

megan-sre: +1 on alerts. Also adding a sticky note: we should make `x-serving-region` available as a first-class column in Console logs (low-effort) so support isn't decoding trace logs for customers.

emily-support: Customer replied — they retried and latency is back to normal, no more 401s. Will close once I log the credit. Thanks everyone. :pray:
